To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

there are 40 key questions that can guide the research on science-policy interface, which can be divided in 6 groups, and that these questions were derived by 52 participants selected from a variety of disciplines and backgrounds, and by using a collaborative procedure.

a collaborative procedure involving 40 experts identified 40 questions that they consider important for understanding the science-policy relationship, and that they expect that research on these questions will improve mutual understanding and effectiveness.

the most important unanswered questions in the science-policy relationship include the effectiveness of science based decision-making structures, the nature and legitimacy expertise, the consequences of changes, such as increasing transparency, choices among different sources, the implications of new ways of characterizing and representing uncertainties and ways in which political processes affect what constitutes authoritative evidence.

the nature of science-policy relationships, the factors that affect them, and the consequences of these factors for the quality, legitimacy and impact of scientific advice to policy.
